title: Tutte’s path theorem for matroids
abstract: Proves the modular-cut path theorem for finite matroids, with reusable rank-partition, hyperplane-separation, relative-complement, indecomposable-cover, and diamond constructions.

informal.TutteFormalization.path_theorem: In a finite connected matroid, any two hyperplanes containing a proper indecomposable flat and lying outside a modular cut are joined by a finite Tutte path all of whose vertices contain that flat and avoid the cut. Consecutive vertices are distinct hyperplanes with indecomposable corank-two intersection; repeated nonconsecutive vertices are permitted.
informal.TutteFormalization.path_theorem_of_indec: In any finite matroid, two hyperplanes containing an indecomposable flat F and lying outside a modular cut are joined by a Tutte path whose vertices contain F and avoid the cut. This strengthens the cited path theorem by requiring only connectedness of the contraction by F; properness of F follows from containment in an endpoint hyperplane.
informal.TutteFormalization.exists_indecomposable: If an indecomposable flat S and a flat U span the ground, every indecomposable flat T contained in both extends inside S to an indecomposable flat R spanning the ground with U, with corank R equal to rank U minus rank T.
informal.TutteFormalization.exists_relative_compl: For nested flats T contained in S, there is a flat U containing T whose intersection with S is T, whose join with S is the ground, and whose corank equals rank S minus rank T.
